# SCI-NOI v0.1 r0.5 Normative Assumptions
Module identity: `SCI-NOI_NORMATIVE_ASSUMPTIONS v0.1/r0.5`
Scientific owner: Grant Wilson. Status: proposed final; not frozen.

`SCI-NOI-ASM-001` Authority is the exact r0.18 packet, r0.3 owner supplement, r0.4 and r0.5 owner directives, and this byte-bound module set; process records add no science.
`SCI-NOI-ASM-002` Numerical GEN remains unavailable until exact PTC coefficient/QC, canonical rational design values, numerical `coverage_cut`, MAP admission, response, profiles, and every parent/plan fact exist.
`SCI-NOI-ASM-003` The real signal and every member share identical occurrences, operator, denominator, support, response, and gates.
`SCI-NOI-ASM-004` Independent symmetric candidate bits belong to the declared ideal randomization model. Exact content-bound disjoint counters and keying supply deterministic replay identity; replay success alone supplies no independence or generator-quality validation.
`SCI-NOI-ASM-005` First acceptance conditional on success is uniform on `A`; the finite cap changes resolution probability only.
`SCI-NOI-ASM-006` Candidate rejection is construction, not a member or failure. Binding completion and member-use predicates are fixed before assignment or assignment-invariant; assignment-dependent failure makes the base method unavailable and cannot select a favorable survivor ensemble.
`SCI-NOI-ASM-007` The fixed parent may contain source and residuals; no physical-noise or significance model is supplied.
`SCI-NOI-ASM-008` r0.18 profiles and Registry objects remain immutable. Proposed r0.5 successors are unevaluable pending owner approval and binding.
`SCI-NOI-ASM-009` Adjacent parents remain immutable; transforms and relearning require external authority and new generations.
`SCI-NOI-ASM-010` Full STD response is unavailable until the complete conditional-second-moment response is separately authorized.
`SCI-NOI-ASM-011` The ideal unconditioned `Uniform(A)` target is retained only under EQ-017. A scientifically required assignment-dependent gate defines a different conditioned law, method, estimator, weights, uncertainty, and claim.
`SCI-NOI-ASM-012` Numerical estimator uncertainty remains unavailable until an exact method supplies it; neither deterministic replay nor a single realized assignment set establishes that uncertainty.
